'''Bettina Eick''' is a German mathematician specializing in computational group theory. She is Professor of Mathematics at the [[Technical University of Braunschweig|Technische Universität (TU) Braunschweig]].

== Life and education ==
Eick was born on May 16, 1968.<ref name="cvweb">{{Cite web |title=CV |url=http://www.iaa.tu-bs.de/beick/cv.html|work=Bettina Eick|publisher=Technische Universität Braunschweig |access-date=7 September 2022}}</ref> She attended the [[RWTH Aachen University|Rheinische-Westfälische Technische Hochschule (RWTH) Aachen]] from 1987 to 1993.<ref name="cv2017">{{cite web|url=http://www.aims-volkswagen-workshops.org/2017/CVs/CV_Eick.pdf|publisher=Africa Institute for Mathematical Sciences|department= AIMS-Volkswagen Stiftung Workshop on Introduction to Computer Algebra and Applications |date=2017|title=Curriculum Vitae (Bettina Eick)|access-date=7 September 2022}}</ref> During that time she spent a year at the Queen Mary and Westfield College (currently known as [[Queen Mary University of London|Queen Mary University London]]).<ref name="cvweb"/> In 1993, she completed her Diplom thesis under the supervision of Joachim Neubüser.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Jahresbericht der Deutschen Mathematiker-Vereinigung|date=17 May 2022|last1=Eick|first1=Bettina|last2=Hulpke|first2=Alexander|last3=Niemeyer|first3=Alice C.|title= Joachim Neubüser (1932 - 2021), Obituary |pages=147–155|doi=10.1365/s13291-022-00255-7|s2cid=248871579 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

In 1996, Eick earned her PhD also at RWTH Aachen under the supervision of Neubüser. Her dissertation was entitled ''Charakterisierung und Konstruktion von Frattinigruppen mit Anwendungen in der Konstruktion endlicher Gruppen'' (''Characterization and Constructions of Frattini Groups with Applications to the Construction of Finite Groups'').<ref name="cv2017"/><ref>{{MathGenealogy| 28986 }}</ref>

== Career ==
Eick began her career with postdoctoral positions at RWTH Aachen and the University of Würzburg.<ref name="cv2017"/> She received her [[habilitation]] at the [[University of Kassel]] in 2001<ref name="cvweb"/> before joining TU Braunschweig.<ref name="cv2017"/>

Eick is known for her work in algorithmic algebra and group theory. Her early work focused on the development of practical algorithms for polycyclic groups and the construction of finite groups. She is one of the main developers of the [[Small groups library|SmallGroups library]]. This database contains, among others, a complete list of all groups of order at most 2000, except for order 1024. The list includes more than 400 million finite groups and is available in the computer algebra systems [[GAP (computer algebra system)|GAP]], [[Magma computer algebra system|Magma]], [[SageMath]], and [[Oscar (computer algebra system)|Oscar]].<ref>{{Cite web |access-date=2022-09-07 |title=Chapter 1: The Small Groups Library | work=The GAP Small Groups Library Documentation| publisher=The GAP Group|last1=Eick|first1=Bettina|last2=O'Brien|first2=Eamonn |url=https://docs.gap-system.org/pkg/smallgrp/doc/chap1.html}}</ref>{{better source needed|reason=this is a primary source, and does not support inclusion in Magma, Sage, and Oscar|date=September 2022}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=GAP (smallgrp)-Contents |url=https://docs.gap-system.org/pkg/smallgrp/doc/chap0.html |access-date=7 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Magma-Documentation |url=https://magma.maths.usyd.edu.au/magma/handbook/text/776 |access-date=7 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Oscar: Computer algebra system |url=https://oscar.computeralgebra.de/ |access-date=7 September 2022}}</ref>

Since 2000, Eick has been a contributor to the "coclass project" that aims to classify groups of prime power order and other nilpotent algebraic objects using [[coclass]] as a primary invariant. In 2005, 2011 and 2017 she was a guest scientist at the University of Auckland working with Eamonn O'Brien and funded by the Feodor Lynen Research Fellowship from the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=SageMath-external packages |url=https://doc.sagemath.org/html/en/reference/spkg/ |access-date=7 September 2022}}</ref>{{citation needed|date=September 2022}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Zealand Association of von Humboldt Fellows |url=https://www.humboldt.org.nz/award/feodor-lynen-fellows/ |access-date=7 September 2022}}</ref>

Eick is a coauthor of the computer algebra system GAP and has been a member of the GAP council since 2001 (chair since 2021).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gap-system.org/Contacts/People/Council/council.html|title=The GAP Council|publisher=The GAP Group|access-date=7 September 2022}}</ref>
